architecture_principles: the unit of decision is an experiment, not a formulation
value of information is computed by a deterministic scientific tool, not by an additional language model
every registered hypothesis carries an explicit pre-result prediction rule and an explicit falsification condition
a measurement that cannot separate any registered hypothesis scores zero discrimination, and that is a scientific result rather than a defect
weight sensitivity is reported as decision stability, never as model confidence
ties in the deterministic layer are reported as ties; the tool must not manufacture a preference it does not have
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
the mechanism question and the Agent framework are separate contributions and are reported separately

candidate_space.rationale: V4 deliberately reuses the byte-identical V3 lattice. Continuous-space optimization and any new wet-lab work are out of scope, so that the measured change between V3 and V4 is the decision object and the VOI layer, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer (including the deterministic VOI tool) -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V4.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime. Its adjudication tests whether a registered hypothesis survives contact with the completed measurement. It is not a contemporaneous pre-experimental record and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_VOI_GUIDED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V4
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
turning the study into a pure AI benchmark
weakening or replacing the rheological mechanism result
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that selects the next formulation x measurement EXPERIMENT by transparent value of information, rather than selecting a formulation candidate alone.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question that the next experiment must answer, then request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations

execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, and the deterministic VOI tool that scores every formulation x measurement experiment card
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value, stating the hypotheses it separates and what each possible outcome would establish
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability of the primary observable, and whether the stated falsification criterion can actually be met by the measurement
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported VOI weight sensitivity and the skeptic's strongest objection
commit to one experiment card, or abstain, and state the acceptance and falsification criteria that will adjudicate it
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card with timestamps, model identifiers and cryptographic hashes of every input

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V4 is an independent architecture. configs/agent_v3.json, prompts/agent_v3_*.txt, src/pur_new/agent_v3.py and every frozen V3 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V4.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards
voi_tool.not_a_posterior: The local design contains six audited realizations and two thermal-hold trajectories. That does not support a calibrated Bayesian expected-information computation, so no posterior probability is fabricated. Weight sensitivity is reported instead.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: Accept the S1C02 reactive-core baseline as consistent with H-CORE if the mean SI_15_60 is between 7.51% and 11.51%, inclusive, and the repeat max-minus-min spread is no greater than 2.00 percentage points.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: If the mean SI_15_60 is below 7.51% and the repeat max-minus-min spread is no greater than 2.00 percentage points, falsify H-CORE at the declared resolution. A mean from 7.51% through 11.51% with spread no greater than 2.00 percentage points supports rather than falsifies H-CORE. A mean above 11.51% with spread no greater than 2.00 percentage points contradicts its numerical prediction but does not meet the registry's one-sided low-drift falsification rule. A repeat spread above 2.00 percentage points falsifies no registered hypothesis because realization-state ambiguity remains. No outcome from this unmodified composition falsifies H-RESIN or H-DUAL.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: Run S1C02::M-REPEAT with three controlled, fully recorded preparations to test realization-state control; after that, use M-HOLD-120 on separately identified E2-derived acrylic-only and minor-tackifier-containing candidates. No eligible modifier-candidate identifier is supplied here, so none is invented.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: Repeat-level SI_15_60 = 100 × (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15 at 120 C, summarized by the arithmetic mean and max-minus-min spread across at least two independent preparations.
judge_normalized.rationale: This experiment directly measures the least-resolved 120 C hold-drift coordinate on the central E2 reactive-core anchor. It is scientifically defensible as a limited probe of H-CORE under sparse evidence, but it is not a mitigation formulation and cannot distinguish resin suppression from a minor-tackifier requirement because both modifier axes are zero.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: I followed the Proposer and Robustness Adjudicator on selecting S1C02::M-HOLD-120 because S1C02 is the measured E2 anchor, lacks hold data, and is more useful than repeating E1/E5 or testing an interpolated core. I followed the Skeptic and Robustness Adjudicator on interpretation: the card is only an H-CORE baseline probe, not evidence for H-RESIN or H-DUAL. I rejected the VOI card's 4.75% cutoff and resin-related language, applying the registered 9.51% prediction with the 2.00-percentage-point resolution instead. The tie among core-only hold cards was broken in favor of S1C02 because it anchors the later modifier design and has documented realization variability.

planner.failure_mode: Viscosity growth during prolonged isothermal melt residence at 120 C (thermal-hold drift), with insufficient evidence that the local modifier design can suppress this growth reproducibly.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The original E5 thermal hold increased by SI_15_60 = 0.5154, or 51.54%, between 15 and 60 min at 120 C, compared with 9.51% for E1. Each profile is represented by only one measured run, so the large drift is observed but its formulation dependence and repeatability remain unresolved.
planner.least_resolved_justification: Temperature response is supported by six-point 80–130 C sweeps, and realized viscosity-level uncertainty is directly documented by three E2 runs with 2.80–3.57-fold max/min spread. In contrast, isothermal behavior is available only for single E1 and E5 runs at 120 C over 15–90 min, with no independent repeats and no hold data for E2 or the candidate modifier axes.
measurement_requirements: Measure each candidate with the matched-window 120 C hold protocol at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min and report SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15.
Use at least two independent preparations per formulation and record process history so formulation effects are not conflated with realization-state displacement.
Include compositions that permit an acrylic-only versus non-zero minor-tackifier comparison at interpretable reactive mass fractions.

Calculate the prospective H-CORE reference E1_drift × phi_r for each measured composition and compare observed drift with both the linear prediction and the registered H-RESIN threshold of less than half that prediction.
Retain the individual time points and repeat-level trajectories rather than reporting only an averaged endpoint, so non-monotonicity and repeat disagreement remain visible.
Preserve source viscosity units and restrict conclusions to the measured 120 C, 15–60 min window without extrapolation.
planner.scientific_question: At matched 120 C residence time, does resin modification reduce SI_15_60 substantially below the reactive-core linear-dilution prediction E1_drift × phi_r, and can an acrylic-only formulation reach that low-drift regime, or is a non-zero minor tackifier-like fraction required? This separates H-CORE from H-RESIN and distinguishes H-DUAL from acrylic-only superlinear suppression.

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: Drift below 4.75% across at least two repeats would be substantially below the registered H-CORE prediction of 9.51% and would falsify H-CORE for this reactive-core composition. Because S1C02 contains neither acrylic-like modifier nor minor tackifier, that result would not establish H-RESIN and would not satisfy the explicit acrylic-only falsification condition for H-DUAL; it would instead reveal an unregistered core-composition or realization-state effect.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: A drift at or above 9.51% would not formally falsify H-RESIN because its falsification condition requires a resin-modified composition. A result close to 9.51% within the 2.00 percentage-point resolution would support H-CORE at the E2 anchor; a result materially above that range would show that reactive mass fraction alone is insufficient. H-DUAL remains untested because neither modifier axis is active.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A repeat-consistent result between 4.75% and 9.51% would indicate partial suppression relative to the linear reference but would meet neither the registered H-RESIN acceptance threshold nor clear support for H-CORE unless it lies within measurement resolution of 9.51%. Repeat disagreement would indicate that process or realization-state uncertainty prevents mechanistic interpretation.

proposer.primary_observable: Directly measured SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, percent, during the matched-window 120 C hold

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: It would directly replicate the E1 hold reference, but E1 already has a measured 120 C trajectory; it adds less new formulation-coordinate information than measuring the untested E2 anchor.
It is a measured reactive-core composition without hold data, but it is not the geometric-center anchor used for the modifier candidate space.
It fills a core-only hold gap but is a larger local core-composition displacement than the E2 anchor and still separates no registered hypothesis pair.
This composition corresponds to the existing high-drift E5 core and would mainly provide replication of an already observed trajectory rather than a new anchor measurement.
It is an interpolated reactive-core point rather than an existing characterized formulation and offers no additional hypothesis discrimination.
It is an interpolated reactive-core point and is less directly useful as the baseline for E2-derived modifier interventions.
It is an interpolated reactive-core point with the same zero pair discrimination and less direct linkage to the registered candidate-space anchor.
It is an interpolated reactive-core point with no modifier axis active and therefore cannot improve mechanistic discrimination over S1C02.

It directly addresses realization-state control, but its primary observable is viscosity-scale spread rather than the least-resolved thermal-hold drift coordinate, so it cannot adjudicate the registered drift hypotheses.

proposer.reasoning: The matched-window hold directly measures the declared failure mode without a regression or transfer model and uses the supported 120 C, 15-60 min window with at least two preparations. S1C02 is inside the characterized local reactive-core family and is the most useful baseline for subsequent modifier tests. However, it lies outside the positive modifier intervention regions because both modifier fractions are zero, and all three registered hypotheses predict 9.51% there. Consequently, this experiment is valuable as a missing anchor and repeatability-sensitive baseline, but it cannot separate H-CORE, H-RESIN, or H-DUAL from one another. Its process-state risk remains moderate because the hold plan repeats preparations but does not itself control all six missing process fields.
proposer.tie_break_justification: S1C02 is the measured E2 reactive-core anchor and geometric center used to construct the modifier candidate space. It has no existing hold data, while its documented 2.80-3.57-fold realization spread makes the required independent hold repeats especially informative. Establishing its 120 C drift baseline is more useful for later comparisons with E2-derived resin-modified candidates than repeating E1 or E5, which already have single-run hold trajectories, or selecting an interpolated core. This choice is not based on card order. All tied cards have identical VOI components and zero registered pair discrimination.

robustness_adjudication.change_from_proposal: Retain the proposed experiment only as a reactive-core baseline. Remove any H-RESIN or H-DUAL acceptance or falsification interpretation, and evaluate H-CORE deviations using the registered 2.00-percentage-point resolution rule rather than treating only drift below 4.75% as falsifying. The next adjudicating experiment should use M-HOLD-120 on an E2-derived acrylic-only and/or minor-tackifier-containing candidate, but no specific eligible candidate identifier is supplied.
residual_decision_risk: The experiment has zero registered hypothesis discrimination because H-CORE, H-RESIN, and H-DUAL all predict 9.51% for this unmodified composition.
S1C02 differs from the single-run E1 reference in NCO:OH ratio and reactive-core composition, so deviation from 9.51% cannot be uniquely attributed to reactive-mass linearity.
The E1 reference is unreplicated and should not be treated as an uncertainty-free benchmark.
M-HOLD-120 does not control process state; six process fields remain missing, and E2 previously showed a 3.5688-fold viscosity spread at 120 C.
Two independent preparations can reveal disagreement but may be insufficient to separate formulation effects from realization-state effects.

The proposed 4.75% H-CORE cutoff is stricter than the registry rule: a repeat-consistent result materially below approximately 7.51% may already contradict the 9.51% prediction beyond the declared 2.00-percentage-point resolution.
The tied top set consists of core-only hold experiments that leave the central modifier hypotheses entangled; the score does not encode a tie-break preference for direct hypothesis separation.
Decision stability under weight perturbation cannot be evaluated because the stability metrics and flip boundaries were withheld.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: S1C02::M-HOLD-120 remains a scientifically useful missing baseline for the E2 reactive-core anchor, and the proposer already states that it separates none of H-CORE, H-RESIN, or H-DUAL. The strongest objection therefore does not invalidate running it for that restricted baseline purpose, but it prevents interpreting any result as evidence for resin suppression or a minor-tackifier requirement. Both modifier axes are zero and all three hypotheses predict 9.51%, so the experiment cannot adjudicate the registered hypothesis set. A subsequent modifier-containing design would be required for adjudication, but the supplied payload does not identify a specific such candidate_id that can be selected without invention.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: The supplied decision-stability report is withheld and provides no top_experiment_set_stability, base_margin_to_first_strictly_lower, or recommendation_flip_boundary values. Therefore, no specific weight perturbation that would change the tied top set, and no assessment of whether such a weighting is scientifically defensible, can be established from the payload. In the visible base scoring, S1C01 through S1C09 with M-HOLD-120 are tied at VOI 0.2435, including the proposal.

skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: The protocol can directly observe whether H-CORE's proposed numerical cutoff of SI_15_60 below 4.75% is met. It cannot meet a valid H-RESIN falsification condition because S1C02 is not resin-modified, and it cannot meet H-DUAL's acrylic-only falsification condition because S1C02 contains no acrylic-like modifier. In addition, the 4.75% H-CORE cutoff is stricter than the registry's beyond-2.00-percentage-point-resolution rule, leaving some registry-inconsistent outcomes classified as intermediate.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Any claim that S1C02::M-HOLD-120 adjudicates resin suppression or tackifier requirement would be unsupported; it is only a reactive-core baseline measurement.
objections.objection: S1C02 has AC1920 = 0.0%, TK100 = 0.0%, and reactive_mass_fraction = 1.0000. The hypothesis_discrimination_detail therefore gives exactly 9.51% for H-CORE, H-RESIN, and H-DUAL, with zero separated pairs. The experiment cannot distinguish any registered hypothesis, although the proposer correctly declares hypotheses_separated = [] and lists all three under hypotheses_not_separated.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A result that contradicts the registered linear-dilution prediction beyond measurement resolution could fail to trigger the registered H-CORE falsification decision.
objections.objection: The proposed H-CORE cutoff of below 4.75% is more stringent than the registered H-CORE falsification rule. With a 9.51% prediction and 2.00 percentage-point resolution, a repeat-consistent result materially below approximately 7.51% could already be beyond declared resolution, yet results from 4.75% to 7.51% are classified as merely intermediate.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A low or high S1C02 drift could be misinterpreted as evidence about dilution or resin mechanisms when it may instead be caused by core composition or stoichiometry.
objections.objection: The comparison reference is the single E1 run at 9.51%, but S1C02 is the E2 core: NCO:OH changes from 1.70 in E1 to 1.80 in E2, MDI fraction changes from 19.2867% to 20.1907%, and the polyol/core composition also changes. Thus phi_r remains 1.0000 while core stoichiometry and composition change. A deviation from 9.51% cannot be uniquely attributed to failure of reactive-mass linearity rather than the changed reactive core.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A repeat-consistent or discordant SI_15_60 result may be assigned to formulation when uncontrolled realization history remains a plausible cause, and no modifier-specific attribution can be made.
objections.objection: M-HOLD-120 does not control process state, six process fields remain missing, and E2 previously showed a 3.5688-fold viscosity spread at 120 C across three realizations. Two independent preparations reveal disagreement but do not by themselves remove uncontrolled preparation-state confounding. Neither modifier axis moves in this experiment, so acrylic suppression, tackifier suppression, and acrylic-versus-tackifier specialization are all unavailable as mechanism attributions; this is not a case where the two modifier axes move together.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: No direct-read interpretability claim is lost, but treating the single-run E1 value of 9.51% as an uncertainty-free benchmark would overstate discrimination.
objections.objection: No objection to the primary observable itself: SI_15_60 is computed directly from measured eta_15 and eta_60 at 120 C, with no regression, extrapolation, or imputation. Retaining the 30 and 45 min points also permits inspection of trajectory shape. The remaining weakness is the unreplicated E1 reference value, not model dependence of the new observable.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A drift at or above 9.51% could be incorrectly reported as falsifying H-RESIN, or a drift below 4.75% as falsifying H-DUAL, despite neither hypothesis being instantiated by the composition.
objections.objection: The VOI card's composite falsification criterion is not attainable for H-RESIN or H-DUAL with S1C02. H-RESIN requires a resin-modified composition, but resin_modified = false and both modifier fractions are zero. H-DUAL requires an acrylic-only composition, but AC1920 is also 0.0%; the card incorrectly calls S1C02 'this acrylic-only composition.' Only the H-CORE numerical event, drift below 4.75%, can actually be produced and evaluated by this protocol.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A core-only rheological anomaly could be presented as evidence for a resin mechanism or molecular encounter-frequency mechanism that the intervention and measurement do not test.
objections.objection: No target-validation identity or unmeasured hold outcome is used, so no outcome leakage is evident. However, the VOI acceptance_criterion says that drift below 4.75% in this unmodified formulation 'accepts H-RESIN over H-CORE.' That exceeds the experiment's scope because no resin is present. The proposer's outcome_interpretation correctly retracts this and says such a result would reveal an unregistered core-composition or realization-state effect. The rheological hold measurement also cannot establish H-RESIN's stated encounter-frequency explanation at a molecular level.

skeptic.recommended_change: Retain S1C02 only as a baseline, not as the adjudicating experiment. Add matched-window M-HOLD-120 tests using the E2-derived core for at least an acrylic-only formulation, a minor-tackifier-containing formulation, and a dual-modifier formulation, with levels chosen so reactive mass fraction and total modifier burden can be compared or explicitly modeled. Include enough acrylic-only dose points to avoid confounding tackifier addition with reduced acrylic loading or extra dilution. Use at least three independently prepared replicates per formulation, fully record and standardize the six missing process fields, and apply each formulation's E1_drift × phi_r reference and registered 2.00-percentage-point resolution rule.
skeptic.strongest_objection: The selected formulation activates neither modifier axis and gives identical 9.51% predictions for H-CORE, H-RESIN, and H-DUAL, so it has zero registered hypothesis discrimination; the card's H-RESIN and H-DUAL falsification language is inapplicable to this composition.

tool_trace.name: get_state_aware_rheology_summary
tool_trace.reason: This must be loaded first to establish the upstream material-state structure, thermal-response regularities, state-calibration implications, and hold-drift design rules before candidate or experiment ranking.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The phosphoric-acid-labelled E1 +P curve is not used in the chemistry-audited primary state model.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.

provenance_audit.reason: The source record is phosphoric-acid-labelled and its additive identity/amount is not represented in formulations.csv; it is retained as sensitivity-only until chemistry is reconciled.

result.source_scope: original pre-validation local measurements with chemistry-comparability audit

The 15% grid level is retained as a lower-bound design point, but the literature denominator for the reported 15% addition level is not treated as an exact total-formulation anchor until reverified.

evidence: PAT_US5932680A: examples around 4.8-6.4% tackifying/hydrocarbon resin and preferred resin range 3-10 wt%
PAT_US20070155859A1: tackifiers/rheology-control agents typically used below about 10 wt%
minor_tackifier_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 5% represents the repeatedly documented minor-resin region and 10% is a conservative coarse upper level.

result.claim_boundary: External examples are analogues. They support candidate-family and coarse-region hypotheses, not an exact optimum for AC1920/TK100 and not a proven local molecular mechanism. The current reconstruction uses only pre-result evidence at runtime; the exact validation coordinates and outcome are excluded from candidate construction, ranking and tie-breaking.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

local_reactive_core_anchor.reason: E2 is the geometric centre of the original five-point local design: 50/50 PPG2000/PDP-70 and NCO:OH=1.80, centered between E1/E3 stoichiometric perturbations and E4/E5 composition perturbations.
local_reactive_core_anchor.stoichiometry_note: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 label applies to the original reactive core. If a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.

top_cards_in_policy_order.acceptance_criterion: Matched 15-60 min drift at 120 C stays below 4.75% across at least two repeats, i.e. below half the linear-dilution prediction of 9.51% implied by a reactive mass fraction of 1.0000. This accepts H-RESIN over H-CORE.
top_cards_in_policy_order.falsification_criterion: H-RESIN is falsified if matched 15-60 min drift is at or above the linear-dilution prediction of 9.51%. H-CORE is falsified if drift falls below 4.75%, a separation larger than the 2.00% resolution threshold. H-DUAL is falsified if this acrylic-only composition reaches the low-drift regime with no minor tackifier present.
